title: Wolves Hall, West Bank lounges and parades
summary: He describes the Wolves Hall and cousins who ran West Bank lounges that hosted Fats Domino and Tommy Ridgley, and how the Wolves marched on holidays.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: They died and the building was sold. Now, my cousin Lloyd Spencer, who at one time had Lloyd's Esquire Lounge, who used to promote Dave Bartholomew and all those guys over there. And incidentally, Lloyd is still alive today. I guess he could fill you in on a lot of people. He had Lloyd's Esquire Lounge over there in Gretna. And then another good friend, I guess I can say he's into my family because Merlin Dennis, who had the Peppermot Lounge in Gretna, he's married to my cousin. He's still alive, but he's kind of ill right now. They could tell you some dynamite stories about jazz and entertainment on the West Bank of the River. And Fats Domino played over there. Tommy Ridgely played over there. Lloyd's Esquire Lounge. Lloyd had them all over there at one time. He's still alive. And so Gretna and Jonestown, I guess you could say that by owning the Wolves, owning their own club, they used to have their committee meetings there. Then they had the Lady Wolves, too, used to come out with them from time to time. And I'm trying to think of, I think Mr. Bolin, a fellow by the name of Bolin was something like one of the committee members because he always would try to get children to be good and come to the hall or something. And they would just have nice affairs over there on the West Bank of the River. Then they had, well, whenever they would tell me about when I would go stay with my Aunt Lillian back in Jonestown, I was a little hesitant about going back there because they had a lady by the name of Patient Evans who kept a big alligator. And when I first saw that alligator, and they were telling me about throwing me in that, when I was a small child, about throwing me in that pit with the alligator being bad. And I said, no, I'm not going back there. But as I grew and got older, it didn't bother me anymore. And Ms. Patient Evans, we got to be very, very good friends. I wasn't worried about the alligator after I started growing up. But the Wolves Hall, the building is still there, but today it's a lounge. It's across from the house where my Aunt Lillian used to live. It's still part of the family homestead. I think it's in the 2100 block, 2200 block of UEP Long Avenue. So you could find it. It's no problem. It's 21 blocks from the river. Yeah, 21 to 22 blocks from the river heading south. Yeah, heading south. But those were the good old days, and they used to march all over Gretchen.
You seem to know just, yeah, that's what I was going to get back to. They marched on certain holidays.

Well, they marched on certain holidays, and they would march sometimes on weekends whenever they feel or believe something was coming up that they wanted to showcase. They would just put on their black outfits with their colorful ribbons and whatnot, and they would just march.
